title: Albert Einstein House, 112 Mercer Street: National Register of Historic Places Inventory -- Nomination Form (National Historic Landmark 76002297)
notes: National Park Service NPGallery copy of the original NRHP/NHL nomination form (Form 10-300) for the Albert Einstein House. The url serves a 6-page scanned PDF (HTTP 200, application/pdf); fetch_snapshot.py has no PDF reader, so the snapshot is the PDF's own text layer extracted with pdftotext (poppler, no layout option), unedited, saved with --method manual. The text layer is OCR and carries OCR errors (for example 'Dim, Germany' for Ulm, 'Rossevelt'); quotes are copied only from passages that read cleanly. G10: the adversary must confirm each quote in the live PDF.

claim: Albert Einstein immigrated to the United States.

evidence.quote: Following the Nazi takeover of political power in Germany in 1933 and the onset of persecution of the German Jews, Einstein renounced his German citizenship and immigrated to the United States to take the position of Professor of Theoretical Physics at Princeton.
Worried about growing Nazi aggression, Einstein immigrated to the United States and accepted a faculty position at Princeton University.

notes: Split from EIN-F-0007 (the 'After the Nazis seized power' wording is Nobel Prize Outreach only). Two holders in different words: LoC item record and DocsTeach (NARA education site, unregistered, secondary).

claim: In 1933 Albert Einstein renounced his German citizenship.

evidence.quote: He became a German citizen in 1914 and remained in Berlin until 1933 when he renounced his citizenship for political reasons

Following the Nazi takeover of political power in Germany in 1933 and the onset of persecution of the German Jews, Einstein renounced his German citizenship and immigrated to the United States to take the position of Professor of Theoretical Physics at Princeton.

notes: Split from EIN-F-0014 without 'for political reasons' (which only the Nobel text and the Franklin Institute text derived from it carry): Nobel Prize Outreach and the Library of Congress each state the 1933 renunciation.

claim: Albert Einstein signed a letter to President Roosevelt.

evidence.quote: Einstein signed a letter that informed President F. D. Roosevelt of the possibility of nuclear bombs, warning that the Germans might try to build them.
He signed a letter to President Roosevelt alerting him to the possibility of the development of atomic weapons.

notes: Split from EIN-F-0089 without the month (no second holder states 'August 1939' with 'signed'): IAS and NPS (Manhattan Project pioneers page) each state it.
